models.summary: Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6 Flash is an efficiency-oriented model for coding and general agent workflows. The official Flash-RL card describes joint training for code, general agents and visual tasks.
strengths: Repository code tasks and tool-driven agent work are documented training and evaluation targets.
The published architecture accepts text, image, video and audio with a long context window.
limitations: Published capabilities describe the model family; each serving provider may expose fewer modalities or a smaller context window.
The cited evaluation is developer-reported and does not establish reliability for every research, planning or writing task.
Xiaomi retained the Flash API identifier after replacing checkpoints with the MOPD update; the hosted checkpoint is not assumed identical to the cited Flash-RL weights.

models.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a compact hybrid reasoning and chat model for specialized agents. NVIDIA publishes coding, tool-use, instruction-following and long-context evaluations.
strengths: Text reasoning, coding and tool-use are documented capabilities.
Thinking can be enabled or disabled through the supported chat template.
limitations: Published results depend on the serving precision, inference settings and evaluation harness; hosted variants are not assumed identical to BF16 reference weights.
The model's training cutoff limits unaided knowledge of later events; current factual research needs external sources.

models.summary: Meituan's LongCat 2.5 Preview is presented as a multimodal model for coding and productivity, with native tool calls and multi-step reasoning.
strengths: The developer identifies code generation, code understanding and automated programming as intended strengths.
The developer documents long-context agent tasks and compatibility with coding-agent clients.
limitations: This is a preview model; the cited product documentation does not establish independent benchmark performance or reliability across all job classes.
Multimodal input and maximum context depend on the actual serving provider's exposed capabilities.
